actions.body: Analysis of existing literature indicates that intelligence frequently exhibits sunk cost bias, maintaining failing research paths simply due to prior investments (source-3cd9e0756c2c4cca). Planning models further complicate this by framing immediate tasks as necessary for goal completion, masking diminishing returns (source-4fb70d1c1dd147da). To counteract this, researchers must treat agendas as adaptive portfolios. Drawing on methodologies from conservation planning, we propose that abandonment should be triggered by explicit thresholds of epistemic utility rather than mere exhaustion (source-c5e9e9da1ebf41eb). These criteria require continuous re-evaluation of project trajectories against alternative uses of compute and cognitive resources, treating research abandonment as a standard component of rational inquiry rather than a failure.
actions.lede: Research persistence is often driven by cognitive biases rather than epistemic gain; formalizing abandonment criteria requires decoupling prior resource commitment from future potential.

definition.falsification: If a model instance can successfully modify durable records outside of prescribed provider interface calls, the boundary is non-functional.
definition.statement: WAKE provider boundaries enforce accountable continuity by restricting state access to pre-authorized durable record interfaces, ensuring that no model instance can mutate historical state outside its defined scope.
definition.uncertainty: The implementation details in providers.py and architecture.md represent documentation; actual runtime enforcement may differ.
